registry: Knowledge Dungeon public media license registry
purpose: Machine-readable provenance for every file under public/assets. `npm run test:licenses` (scripts/check-cc0-assets.mjs) validates this file, recomputes every checksum from the bytes on disk, and fails if any media file is unregistered, misclassified, or admitted to the default PixiJS bundle without CC0 or procedural provenance.
owner: Phase 8, CC0 media licensing half. The Cozy design tokens are owned separately in src/theme/.
privacy: This file contains asset paths, asset ids, license facts, and checksums. It contains no learner data, and the checker never prints a registry value: it prints only paths, ids, and field names, and withholds any identifier that does not match its expected shape.

license.appliesTo: Only entries classified cc0-approved or procedural. Nothing else may claim it.

planSections: Phase 8 scope: "Classify every existing asset as approved CC0, procedural, or legacy unverified."

Plan section 10.3: CI must reject any newly registered media lacking an id and path, a creator or source, a source URL where applicable, the exact CC0-1.0 identifier, a license URL, a retrieval or creation date, a SHA-256 checksum, or a modification record.
Plan section 10.3: unverified legacy assets may remain available to the legacy renderer during migration but must not be included in the default PixiJS bundle.
ADR 002 Decision 5 states the same media policy.

classificationRules.cc0-approved: Media verified as CC0 1.0 with full provenance. May enter the default PixiJS bundle. No entry carries this class today: nothing in this repository has a verified CC0 grant, and an unverified asset must never be recorded as approved.
classificationRules.procedural: Generated by a committed script, so no third-party license attaches. The generation recipe is recorded and the generating script must exist on disk. May enter the default PixiJS bundle.
classificationRules.legacy-unverified: Pre-existing media whose license cannot be verified. Never Pixi-eligible. Available to the legacy renderer only, under the `retention` policy, and dropped when Phaser is removed in Phase 24.
classificationRules.repository-authored: A non-media file authored in this repository rather than imported. Recorded as a fourth class because the plan taxonomy is a media taxonomy and the honest classification of this repository's own credits file is neither CC0 nor procedural nor unverified: it is MIT-licensed by the repository LICENSE. Non-media only, and never Pixi-eligible.
classificationRules.repositoryOrigin: Most of the legacy SVGs were first committed by an in-repository feature commit rather than by the repo-dungeon import commit, so they are not claimed as imported material. They are still not approved: the repository LICENSE is MIT, and MIT is not CC0-1.0, so there is no verified CC0 provenance. The copyright holder can make an asset Pixi-eligible either by re-licensing it to CC0-1.0 and recording that grant here, or by replacing it. This registry never records a license that was not actually stated.

policy.pixiBundleRule: Only cc0-approved and procedural entries may be members of a bundle, and only entries in an approved bundle path may declare membership. Anything else fails, which is what keeps unverified legacy media out of the default PixiJS bundle.
policy.declaredEmptyBundleRule: A bundle may be declared before it has any media, and five are: common, village, dungeon, fishing, and share-card. A declared-empty bundle has zero members today and the path it reserves does not exist on disk, which is the honest state of Phase 10 - its non-goals exclude final world-specific asset production, and cc0-approved is 0, so there is no verified grant to admit. The reserved path is a policy, not a provenance claim: it declares where the bundle's media may live, so that the gate's unapproved-media tripwire (an unverified or unregistered file appearing under an approved bundle path fails) is armed before the first file lands rather than being retrofitted afterwards. It is deliberately not public/assets/sprites/, where the 90 legacy-unverified files live: admitting that tree to any bundle would fail the gate, and it must keep failing.
policy.dateKindRule: created and retrieved are the plan's creation and retrieval dates and are mandatory for approved classes. legacy-unverified entries use introduced-in-repository, because the upstream creation or retrieval date is unknown and recording a guess would be a false provenance claim.

paletteNote: PROVISIONAL placeholder values for the Phase 8 procedural set only. src/theme/ is the source of truth, and these are art inputs rather than a second token declaration: every family and token name below is a verbatim copy of the matching COZY_COLOR_FAMILIES entry in src/theme/cozyTokens.ts, for the families the plan names (parchment, moss, berry, ink, firelight) and only for the tokens the generator actually reads. The generator paints from this block, so a generated file cannot drift from the shipped Cozy palette, and tests/phase8/cozy-palette-alignment.test.ts fails if a value here stops matching the token module. Tokens the token module defines but this placeholder set does not read (parchment.ink, ink.base, ink.raised, ink.sunken, ink.line, ink.text, firelight.spark) are deliberately absent rather than approximated. Phase 10 declared the five further bundle sets - common, village, dungeon, fishing, and share-card - and, as its non-goals require, produced no world-specific media for them, so this placeholder art and these provisional colours are still the only art a Pixi bundle may ship. The real art is later work, and a phase that produces it must record the recipe here, keep the tokens aligned with src/theme/cozyTokens.ts, and never reclassify the 90 legacy-unverified files to get there.

assets.role: Build output listing every SVG under this directory with its parsed dimensions. Written by the sprite-manifest Vite plugin and read by the Express server and the upload-boundary privacy test.
assets.creator: Knowledge Dungeon procedural generator (scripts/generate-sprite-manifest.mjs)
assets.source: Generated in this repository by a committed script. It is an index of dimensions, not third-party media.

sourceUrlNotApplicable.reason: Generated by a committed script in this repository; there is no external source to cite.

generation.recipe: Walk public/assets recursively for .svg files, parse each width and height from the viewBox or the width and height attributes (64x64 when unparseable), derive a category from the directory path, sort by path, and emit a generatedAt timestamp.
generation.checksum: A pinned checksum is impossible: the manifest records a generatedAt timestamp, so its bytes change on every run. It is gitignored, so on a fresh checkout it may legitimately be absent. It is verified semantically instead: the manifest's sprite path set must equal the set of SVGs discovered under public/assets.
